questions.question: The heading of this statement must read:
options: For the year ended 28 February — it covers a stretch of time, not a single day

questions.question: Gross operating income of R1 152 000 consists of:
options: Sales of R2 880 000 less all expenses
Gross profit of R1 080 000 plus other operating income of R72 000

questions.question: Operating profit of R552 000 less the interest expense of R24 000 gives:
options: Net profit for the year of R528 000

questions.question: Partners' salaries, interest on capital and the bonus do not appear in this statement because:
options: They were paid in cash during the year
They are too small to disclose
They belong in the trading account
They are appropriations of profit, dealt with after the last line, inside the notes

questions.question: Trade and other receivables include net trade debtors of:
options: R60 800 — debtors of R64 000 less the R3 200 provision for bad debts

questions.question: The Sisonke Bank loan appears under non-current liabilities at:
options: R185 000 — the closing balance, with the year's capitalised interest already inside it

questions.question: Total equity and liabilities of R1 175 400 must equal:
options: Total assets of R1 175 400 — the accounting equation in published form

questions.question: An item is classified as CURRENT when it:
options: Becomes cash or falls due within twelve months

questions.question: Land and buildings show no depreciation because:
options: Land does not wear out, and historical cost holds it at what it cost
The property is too valuable to depreciate
The partners decided against it this year

questions.question: Vehicles: cost R285 000, accumulated depreciation at the start R114 000, current depreciation R57 000. The closing carrying value is:
options: R114 000 — cost less closing accumulated depreciation of R171 000

questions.question: The three closing carrying values — R560 000, R114 000 and R81 000 — must add up to:
options: R755 000, the fixed assets line on the face of the statement

questions.question: The depreciation policy is written into the note in words because:
options: Consistency requires the same method year after year, and readers must know which method the figures obey

subtopics.title: The Notes: Capital, Current Accounts and the Principles

questions.question: The capital accounts note shows no movement this year because:
options: Fixed capital moves only on a formal decision between the partners, and none was taken
The bookkeeper left out the entries
Capital always follows profit up and down

questions.question: Venter's opening balance in the current accounts note is shown as:
options: A negative R6 800, because she owed the business at the start of the year

questions.question: The closing balances of R48 100 and R41 700 in the current accounts note reach the face of the statement as:
options: The R89 800 current accounts line inside owners' equity

questions.question: Valuing everything on the assumption that the shop keeps trading is the principle of:

subtopics.title: The Highlights Reel and the Team Photo

questions.question: The highlights reel and the team photo stand for:
options: The income statement covering the whole year, and the financial position statement freezing one day
Two versions of the same statement
The budget and the actual figures

questions.question: The photo rule says:
options: The photo must be retaken monthly
Both rows must stand equally tall — R1 175 400 owned, R1 175 400 claimed

questions.question: A business needs BOTH statements because:
options: One goes to the bank and one to SARS
Each is blind where the other sees — profit says nothing about paying next month's accounts, and a full bank account might be borrowed money
They repeat the same information twice

subtopics.title: The Fine Print That Shows the Workings

questions.question: The relationship between the face and the notes is:
options: Face for the conclusion, note for the proof — and they must meet to the rand
The face repeats the notes word for word

questions.question: The fixed assets note reaches R755 000 by adding:
options: R560 000 plus R114 000 plus R81 000 — the closing carrying values

questions.question: The face shows debtors at R60 800 rather than R64 000 because:
options: R3 200 was received after year end
The R3 200 provision dims the figure to what will honestly be collected

questions.question: The capital note standing perfectly still all year demonstrates:
options: That planted money is meant to stand still, and the note publicly certifies that it did
That the business is in trouble
That the note was completed wrongly

questions.question: Venter's column runs from minus R6 800 through earnings of R265 500 and drawings of R217 000 to close at:
options: Plus R41 700 — out of the red, with the business owing her

questions.question: Publishing the opening debit balance instead of hiding it reflects:
options: Honest disclosure — the statements hide nothing, in the spirit of prudence and faithful presentation

questions.question: Keeping the shop's books apart from the partners' wallets is the principle of:
